technologies.how: Messages, enums, oneof fields, maps, services, streaming RPC, and deterministic serialization.
technologies.name: Protocol Buffers
technologies.what: Defines language-neutral schemas for compact binary messages and RPC services.
technologies.when: Use when multiple languages need one evolvable typed contract.
technologies.where: Service contracts, telemetry, receipts, registries, and cross-language mission envelopes.
technologies.why: Field-numbered schemas preserve compatibility and generate implementations across ecosystems.

technologies.how: Tables, structs, vectors, unions, namespaces, and generated builders/accessors.
technologies.name: FlatBuffers
technologies.what: Defines binary objects that can be read directly from a buffer without full unpacking.
technologies.when: Use when read latency and allocation avoidance dominate and schema evolution remains required.
technologies.where: Games, mobile state, telemetry, embedded inference, and latency-sensitive local IPC.
technologies.why: Generated accessors traverse the serialized buffer in place, reducing parsing and copying.

technologies.how: Structs, unions, interfaces, capabilities, promises, and schema evolution.
technologies.name: Cap'n Proto
technologies.what: Combines zero-copy serialization with capability-oriented RPC.
technologies.when: Use when serialized messages and authority-bearing RPC references must share one model.
technologies.where: Low-latency distributed systems, secure object capabilities, storage engines, and agent IPC.
technologies.why: It reads wire-format objects directly and encodes access through explicit capabilities.

technologies.how: Modules, always blocks, nonblocking assignments, wires, registers, and testbenches.
technologies.name: Verilog
technologies.what: Describes synthesizable digital logic at register-transfer level.
technologies.when: Use when the output must become gates, registers, and wires rather than software instructions.
technologies.where: FPGA prototypes, ASIC blocks, counters, pipelines, and arithmetic units.
technologies.why: It gives deterministic cycle-level hardware structure with broad tool support.

technologies.how: always_ff/always_comb, interfaces, packages, assertions, classes, and constrained random verification.
technologies.name: SystemVerilog
technologies.what: Extends Verilog with richer RTL, interfaces, assertions, and verification constructs.
technologies.when: Use when hardware design needs stronger typing, interfaces, or executable assertions.
technologies.where: ASIC/FPGA design, protocol interfaces, constrained verification, and accelerator pipelines.
technologies.why: It unifies synthesizable RTL with powerful verification semantics and industry tooling.

technologies.how: Entities, architectures, processes, signals, generics, packages, and assertions.
technologies.name: VHDL
technologies.what: Describes strongly typed concurrent hardware with explicit packages and timing semantics.
technologies.when: Use when hardware correctness, strong typing, and long-lived certification-oriented design dominate.
technologies.where: Aerospace, defense, FPGA control logic, safety-critical digital systems, and reusable IP.
technologies.why: Its explicit type system and deterministic concurrency support highly reviewable RTL.

technologies.how: Modules, Bundles, Decoupled interfaces, parameters, generators, and FIRRTL lowering.
technologies.name: Chisel
technologies.what: Uses Scala to construct parameterized hardware generators that emit synthesizable RTL.
technologies.when: Use when hardware should be generated from reusable abstractions rather than copied RTL.
technologies.where: RISC-V processors, reusable accelerators, networks-on-chip, and parameterized hardware families.
technologies.why: It brings types, functions, testing libraries, and parameterization to hardware construction.
